name: Baltimore Club
sources: style-research-extended vol.4 jersey-club — "Two neighbouring archetypes are recommended and do not exist in this app: `baltimore-club` and `philly-club`… Rod Lee, K-Swift and the Baltimore founders collective should move to `baltimore-club`"

style-research-extended vol.4 jersey-club — tempo: the Baltimore parent is documented at "tempos around 130 beats per minute"; use 130–134 for Baltimore-facing material and 135–140 for Jersey/Philly-facing

style-research-extended vol.4 jersey-club — Jersey's documented divergence from Baltimore is "harder kicks and chop the samples up a lot more", where Baltimore's counterpart signature is "a lot of horns"

style-research-extended vol.4 jersey-club — the break lane: "simple snippets on a repeated loop", a drawn-out 16-count breakbeat sample, i.e. a 2-bar break against a 1-bar kick figure; keep the break's own ghost snares
style-research-extended-4 vol.4 header — the divergences specified: 130 flat, 8/4 two-bar unit, softer kick, horn stabs
notes: The parent of the whole Baltimore→Jersey line, authored as its own archetype at last. ⛔ **Four sourced divergences from `jersey-club`, and every one of them is a subtraction.** (1) **130 flat** — the band is 128–134 where Jersey runs 130–145 and centres at 138, and the narrowness *is* the parameter. (2) **A softer kick.** Jersey's own documented divergence from Baltimore is *"harder kicks and chop the samples up a lot more"*, so this lane sits below the five-kick bar that `jersey_club_runs_the_densest_kick_in_the_dataset` pins: four to a bar, less syncopated, and locked less tightly to the 808. (3) **Horn stabs where Jersey has chops** — the research gives *"a lot of horns"* as Baltimore's counterpart signature, so `melody.timbreHint` is `horn_stab` and the melodic part is a short answered figure rather than a transposed speech fragment. (4) **A two-bar break unit against a one-bar kick figure**: the flagship record loops *"a drawn-out 16-count breakbeat sample"*, so the ghosts stay in — `snare.ghost.prob` is 0.55, the highest in the club family, because the research says to *keep the break's own ghost snares rather than quantising them out*. ⚠ **Harmony is near-absent and that is a rule, not a gap.** The research is explicit for this whole lane: *"There is no documented chord vocabulary… expect a static single chord or a 1-bar two-chord oscillation, held for the entire record. Do not generate progressions here."* So `maxChords` is 2, the vamp carries almost all the weight, and the extensions are plain. ⚠ **The hat lane is deliberately thin.** *"No source in the Baltimore→Jersey line names a hat pattern as a genre signature… Default the hat lane OFF."* This engine has no way to author a lane off, so it is authored as sparse straight eighths with no rolls — and `rolls.freqPerBar` at 0.05 is what keeps a roll vocabulary the research does not describe from arriving anyway. ⚠ **The kick-lane-only swing is NOT expressible and is not faked.** The research asks for 0% swing globally with 8–16% applied *to the kick lane alone, and only to the middle hit of a cluster*. `session.swing` is one grid for the whole track here, so it is left straight at 0.50: a global 0.58 would swing the break, the hats and the melody, which is the opposite of what the source describes. The shuffled cluster is carried instead by `kick.tresilloBias` and the anchors. ⚠ **Nothing was moved onto this model.** The research names Rod Lee, K-Swift and the Baltimore founders collective as the roster that should move here from `jersey-club`, and `jersey-club` still carries its own `baltimore` mode. Both are migrations — a model's `extends`, a mode's removal and a producer's genre are things saved projects reproduce from — and they belong in their own change. ⚠ **INFERRED, hence `medium`.** Sourced: the tempo band, the softer kick, the horns, the break unit, the ghost-snare rule, the hat rule and the harmony rule. Inferred: every velocity tier, every register, the key and scale lists, the `intervals`/`contour` split and the mode names.
